answer: The nadir detector writes to tundra, and willow exposes every merge. A farm scripting its whole fleet fires them together, thus the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 236 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. Submissions that land within 202 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 3 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
